title: Program terminates with pending promises
body:
Take a file fetch.js with content:
```js
fetch("https://www.google.com/").then(x=>console.log(x));
```
Executing with `bun run fetch.js` terminates without any logging while doing `deno run fetch.js` prints the actual content of the response.

Other problem, adding await in front of everything, like:
```js
await fetch("https://www.google.com/").then(x=>console.log(x));
```
prints
```
[0.05ms] "node_modules.bun" - 1 modules, 1 packages
[native code]
```
instead of the relevant response.

I want to evaluate Bun, and I thought to start with the test suite of one of my Node.js packages.  The tests are invoked using Mocha.

As you'll see there are some incompatibilities in the `process` object.  One is an issue which must be handed off to the Yargs team.

Mocha has a command installed - `node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha` that is installed in `node_modules/.bin`.  The script with no extension on the end is not recognised:

title: Slow down when use `await`

labels.name: performance
labels.description: An issue with performance

body: ### Version 0.1.1 ### Platform Darwin Salt.local 21.5.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.5.0: Tue Apr 26 21:08:37 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.121.3~4/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 arm64 ### What steps will reproduce the bug? Bun is slowed down while using `await` keyword. TLDR; [Reproducible repo](https://github.com/SaltyAom/issue-bun-slow-async) In the real-world app, `async` is required (eg. querying from a database). However, using it in Bun, for some reason slowed down the execution by at least 2 times. To reproduce, let's create 2 file serving HTTP, and loadtest it. ```typescript // sync.ts const handle = () => new Response("Hi") export default { port: 8080, fetch: handle } // async.ts const handle = async () => new Response("Hi") export default { port: 8080, fetch: async () => await handle() } ``` Result: ### However, it runs fast if we don't use `await` Let's edit `async.ts` to return the async function **without await**. ```typescript // ? Will not defers const handle = async () => new Response("Hi") export default { port: 8081, fetch: handle } ``` Although, we can work around it by not using `await` keyword or using `Promise.resolve`, it doesn't offer a good Developer Experience, because we can't `unwrap` the value without using then. In the real-world app, the developer will **have to** unwrap the value and performs some action on it. This situation will have the most problem affecting significant performance when using with Bun as HTTP web server. Here's [reproducible repo](https://github.com/SaltyAom/issue-bun-slow-async) if you want to test the problem. ### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition? Always reproducible when using `await` on any platform. ### What is the expected behavior? Bun shouldn't be slowed down by a lot when performing `await` ### What do you see instead? Quote from `What steps will reproduce the bug?` Serving sync, and async server, then perform loadtest, the server is slowed down. However, if we remove `await` but remain `async`, the speed goes up again. ### Additional information The performance slowed down is vary, this problem is tested on: - MacOS with Apple Silicon Chip (M1 Max 32 core) - Darwin Salt.local 21.5.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.5.0: Tue Apr 26 21:08:37 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.121.3~4/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 arm64 - Slowed down by 2.5x - WSL Debian 11 (AMD Ryzen 5 3500X) - Linux Chiffon 4.19.1280microsoft-standard `#1` SMP Tue Jun 23 12:58:10 UTC 2020 x86_64 GNU/Linux - Slowed down by 1.5x

body:
### Version

0.6.3

### Platform

`Linux DESKTOP-A7ND7QS 5.10.102.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP Wed Mar 2 00:30:59 UTC 2022 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Take the following `sample.ts` file and run with `bun run sample.ts`:
```ts
import path from 'path';

function WSLSafePath(patharg: string): string {
    if (!process.env.WSL_DISTRO_NAME) return patharg; // Comment out this line to test outside of WSL
    const parsed = path.win32.parse(patharg);
    console.dir(parsed);
    return path.posix.join('/mnt/', parsed.root[0]!.toLowerCase(), parsed.dir.slice(parsed.root.length), parsed.base);
}

const FILEPATH: string = WSLSafePath('C:/foo/bar/baz/myfile.jpeg');
console.log(FILEPATH);
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always

### What is the expected behavior?

Output from `ts-node sample.ts`:
```js
{
  root: 'C:/',
  dir: 'C:/foo/bar/baz',
  base: 'myfile.jpeg',
  ext: '.jpeg',
  name: 'myfile'
}
/mnt/c/foo/bar/baz/myfile.jpeg
```

### What do you see instead?

Output from `bun run sample.ts`:
```js
{
  dir: "C:/foo/bar/baz",
  root: "",
  base: "myfile",
  name: "myfile.jpeg",
  ext: ".jpeg"
}
```
Followed by a `TypeError` for trying to access `toLowerCase` of `root[0]` which is `undefined` due to `root` being an empty string.

### Additional information

`parsed.dir` -> OK
`parsed.ext` -> OK
`parsed.root` -> Empty when it shouldn't be (Expected drive letter)
`parsed.base` -> Incorrectly swapped with `parsed.name`
`parsed.name` -> Incorrectly swapped with `parsed.base`

Updated for Bun v0.6.3 (issue persists)

labels.name: bug

body:
### Version

0.1.5

### Platform

Darwin MacBook-Pro-2.local 21.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.6.0: Sat Jun 18 17:07:25 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.140.41~1/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

`bun create react`

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Every time.

### What is the expected behavior?

Should generate output that meets accessibility guidelines.

### What do you see instead?

Two errors:

- Document should have one main landmark
- Page should contain a level-one heading

### Additional information

This just makes me sad. It is 2022! Are we really still using templates that create output with obvious and easily-fixed accessibility issues? Do we really just not give a shit about accessibility at all? Doesn't anyone check this?

The template already uses CSS for styling, so why would you choose an h3 heading instead of h1? The only reason could be to set font size, **which should be set with CSS**. Sorry, but this was well known two decades ago.

And then to use a bland div element without a role instead of a true landmark. Come on!

This is easily fixed. Change the h3 element to h1 and set the size you want in CSS. You set font-size on the header with `font-size: calc(10px + 2vmin);`. Surely you can get this right.

Then either change `<div className="App">` to `<main className="App">` or give it a role: `<div className="App" role="main">` (in which instance the header element needs to be changed, but then it is not really a "header" is it?).

Done. I haven't tried the other templates but I suspect they have the same problems. If the templates **start** with crap HTML, how many devs will bother to fix the HTML? How many will got on to build crap, inaccessible web apps?

Please. Get Bun off on the right footing. [Learn more](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/).

title: ES Modules: Cannot resolve own specifier

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### Version

0.1.10

### Platform

Darwin Lewiss-MacBook-Air.local 21.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.6.0: Wed Aug 10 14:28:35 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.141.5~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T8101 arm64

### Repro

https://replit.com/@ctjlewis/bun-self-resolve

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

An ES Module attempting to resolve its own module specifier will fail to do so. You can see in the repro above that the standard TSC + Node flow does resolve the module's self-reference successfully.

I was initially unsure whether to file this as a bug or a feature request, but ultimately since Bun reuses the package.json standard, [it is expected behavior](https://twitter.com/oven_sh/status/1562248120611885056?s=20&t=6n9WT1t9KiLua2Q48UMN3g) that it supports Node-like ESM resolution and not throw in this case.

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Per the specification, self-resolution only happens for ES modules with [conditional exports](https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#conditional-exports) enabled via the `exports` field in their package.json.  This is very common for supporting backwards compatibility for CJS and is also [encouraged for pure ESM](https://github.com/tsmodule/tsmodule).

### What is the expected behavior?

An ES Module importing a named module that is equal to its own name (the `name` in its package.json), then it should resolve to itself. 

---

See: https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#resolver-algorithm-specification

**PACKAGE_SELF_RESOLVE**(_packageName_, _packageSubpath_, _parentURL_)

  1. Let _packageURL_ be the result of **LOOKUP_PACKAGE_SCOPE**(_parentURL_).
  
  2. If _packageURL_ is **null**, then
    1. Return **undefined**.
  
  3. Let _pjson_ be the result of **READ_PACKAGE_JSON**(_packageURL_).
  
  4. If _pjson_ is **null** or if _pjson.exports_ is **null** or **undefined**, then
    1. Return **undefined**.
  
  5. If _pjson.name_ is equal to _packageName_, then
    1. Return the result of **PACKAGE_EXPORTS_RESOLVE**(_packageURL_, _packageSubpath_, _pjson.exports_, _defaultConditions_).
  
  6. Otherwise, return **undefined**.


### What do you see instead?

```
error: Could not resolve: "bun-self-resolve". Maybe you need to "bun install"?
import { test } from "bun-self-resolve";
```

### Additional information

_No response_

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

0.2.2 (fyi I have also verified this behaviour exists on canary builds 0.3.0)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 21.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.6.0: Mon Aug 22 20:17:10 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.140.49~2/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64 i386

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

I've noticed a difference in how Node and Bun (specifically the node:events polfil) handle (or don't handle, I guess) exceptions which are re-thrown from within an error handler.

Both Bun and Node seem to catch the error and print it out to console, but Node exits with an error code (which I think is the expected behaviour). I thought this might have been a difference between how bun and node handle unhandled exceptions/errors in general (legacy node would not exit), I have tested this back to Node v12 and the behaviour is consistent within Node - it will print the error to the console and exit with an error code (1)

I have created a repo here which reproduces the behaviour above: https://github.com/dominicporteous/bun-node-events

By running the test script within `./test` you can see the difference in how Bun and Node handle the unhandled error within the event emitter.

event.throws.js
```
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import process from 'process';

const main = (silent) => {

    const e = new EventEmitter();

    e.on('error', (err) => {

        silent ? '' : console.log('caught err, will rethrow', err)

        throw err

    })

    e.emit('error', new Error('Firing error'))

}

export default main

if (process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
    main()
}
```

test
```
#/usr/bin/env bash

echo -e "\nRunning file..."
echo -e "\n===============================\n\n"
cat event.throws.js
echo -e "\n\n===============================\n\n"

echo "NODE_VERSION=$(node -v)"
echo "BUN_VERISON=$(bun -v)"

echo -e "\n\n"

BUN_EXIT="$(bun event.throws.js 1> /dev/null; echo "$?")"
NODE_EXIT="$(node event.throws.js 1> /dev/null; echo "$?")"

echo "BUN_EXIT=$BUN_EXIT"
echo "NODE_EXIT=$NODE_EXIT"
```

title: Fix throwing `error: not an error` when calling `db.run(" ")`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: bun:sqlite
labels.description: Something to do with bun:sqlite

body:
Currently `SQLITE_OK` return status from `sqlite3` causes an error to be thrown in several instances (at least potentially). One such instance is when a string that contains only whitespace characters is passed, it ends up not creating a `statement` and so it throws an error saying `not an error` (`SQLITE_OK` result message from `sqlite3` lib). 

We should:
1. Fix instances where `SQLITE_OK` could potentially show up but is not currently checked for.
2. Differentiate between an actual error from parsing a statement and an empty query, and throw an error telling the user the query is probably empty.

title: bun does not follow PromiseResolveThenableJob of the spec

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: bun.js
labels.description: Something to do with a Bun-specific API

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

0.5.7

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 5.15.63 x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/runtime-architecture-pgzmzc

```sh
> cat test.js 
"const promise = Promise.resolve();/
promise.then(() => console.log(1));/
new Promise((resolve) => resolve(promise)).then(() => console.log(3));/
new Promise((resolve) => promise.then(resolve)).then(() => console.log(2));"
> bun test.js
1
3
2
```

### What is the expected behavior?

1
2
3

### What do you see instead?

1
3
2

### Additional information

Browsers and node shows `1, 2, 3`.

According to [the spec](https://262.ecma-international.org/6.0/#sec-promiseresolvethenablejob) the behaviour of passed promise to a resolve function and pass resolve function to "then" of promise is different.

From my personal perspective it isn't obvious and weird, but I assumes an engine should follow the spec.

title: AOT compilation with Hop.js, instead of JSC JIT

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun still has the same problem of not being able to AOT compile its programs, as in any other JIT implementation of JS.

With AOT compiled JS plus the ultra-fast standard library from Bun, we could reach a theoretically oasis for JS, being finally able to use it universally, including native iOS applications, low-latency scenarios like command line apps, and many more.

Additionally:
 - the startup time on serverless would reach a whole new level
 - the memory usage would reduce even more _(perhaps on various scales of magnitude, as presented in https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iY1EXHQ6IeQ)_

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Using Hop.js ([manuel-serrano/hop](https://github.com/manuel-serrano/hop)) as an AOT compiled JS implementation as a replacement of JSC to solve such problem and bringing (in some cases) an additional increase of performance.

### What alternatives have you considered?

There were some attempts to AOT compile javascript, but they were incomplete _or_ not performant, losing badly from JIT implementations.

Hop.js is a profound research on AOT JS which finally brings the same performance than the JIT counterparts (on average) and adds the benefits of independent and really compiled binaries, as in C/C++, instead of fake compilation like on `pkg` and `bkg`.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: bundler
labels.description: Something to do with the bundler

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Sometimes when develop you want to debug your code and you use `console` methods to show debug messages. You could overwrite `console` which is probably not the best practice by using any env var.

But when you build for production maybe it is a good idea delete all `console` messages.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

A flag/option in `Bun.build` to delete all `console` calls. Maybe would be better choose which are those you want to delete.


Delete all messages:
```javascript
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ['./index.tsx'],
  outdir: './build',
  console: true
});
```

Keep or delete specific messages, not sure which logic would be better:

```javascript
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ['./index.tsx'],
  outdir: './build',
  console: ['info', 'table', 'log'], // Keep all others console methods.
});
```


### What alternatives have you considered?

Override console methods by using env var for non development environments.

I tried select example with node. This is what is showed when execute:

I have to press enter again to finish the program:

title: Bun does not print an error’s `cause` when outputting an error.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

0.6.9

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 22.5.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`a.js`:

```js
try {
  throw new Error('Inner')
} catch (e) {
  throw new Error('Outer', { cause: e })
}
```

`bun a.js`

### What is the expected behavior?

The error log should display the cause of an error, to make debugging easy:

```
Error: Outer
      at /private/tmp/a/a.js:4:8
  [cause]: Error: Inner
        at /private/tmp/a/a.js:2:8
}
```

For example, this is Node.js output

```
/private/tmp/a/a.js:4
  throw new Error('Outer', { cause: e })
  ^

Error: Outer
    at Object.<anonymous> (/private/tmp/a/a.js:4:9)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1218:14)
    ... 4 lines matching cause stack trace ...
    at node:internal/main/run_main_module:23:47 {
  [cause]: Error: Inner
      at Object.<anonymous> (/private/tmp/a/a.js:2:9)
      at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1218:14)
      at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1272:10)
      at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1081:32)
      at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:922:12)
      at Function.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (node:internal/modules/run_main:81:12)
      at node:internal/main/run_main_module:23:47
}
```

### What do you see instead?


```
1 | try {
2 |   throw new Error('Inner')
3 | } catch (e) {
4 |   throw new Error('Outer', { cause: e })
            ^
error: Outer
      at /private/tmp/a/a.js:4:8
```

### Additional information

Right now I have to do this. IMO developers shouldn’t have to write such things by themselves as it should be handled automatically by the runtime (like Node):

```ts
function logError(error: string) {
    console.log(error)
    if (error.cause) {
        console.error(error.cause)
        if ((error.cause as any).cause) {
             console.error((error.cause as any).cause)
        }
    }
}
```

I have a telegram bot written in typescript that I've been running fine with bun up until v0.6.9.

I've identified the problematic code in this file: https://github.com/TommasoAmici/sandro-cois-bot/blob/main/src/plugins/loc.ts

```ts
const mbxGeocoding = require("@mapbox/mapbox-sdk/services/geocoding");
import { Context, HearsContext } from "grammy";
import cfg from "../config";

const geocodingClient = mbxGeocoding({ accessToken: cfg.mapboxToken });

const makeMapboxScreenshot = (coord: number[]): string =>

export const location = async (ctx: HearsContext<Context>) => {
  const query = ctx.match[1];
  geocodingClient
    .forwardGeocode({ query: query, limit: 1 })
    .send()
    .then(async (response: unknown) => {});
};
```

I haven't been able to make a minimal reproduction as a bot with only this function works properly, but when I run it with the entire codebase it fails.

No error

```
error: script "start" exited with code 11 (SIGSEGV)
```


### Additional information

I realize this is not easy to reproduce because it requires a few API tokens and to checkout a non-minimal reproduction, so if you could point me to some docs on how to produce a more meaningful bug report, I'll be happy to help.

title: Bun equivalent of Node's `--preserve-symlinks`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: node.js
labels.description: Compatibility with Node.js APIs

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

0.7.3

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 22.2.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Symlink a file that imports from another module using relative paths, e.g.
```ts
// src/foo/file.ts (symlink'd from src/bar/file.ts)
import { value } from './file2'
console.log(value)
```

This will import from `/src/bar/file2.ts` however TS thinks it is loading `/src/foo/file2.ts` leading to a mismatch between what my editor thinks `value` is vs what it actually is at runtime.

### What is the expected behavior?

Bun should support some way to opt-in to the TypeScript behavior, the equivalent of Node's `--preserve-symlinks` flag.

### What do you see instead?

Mismatch between runtime value and what TS thinks at edit/compile time.

### Additional information

_Note: The following is what I posted on Discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/876711213126520882/1138128619768647680/1138128619768647680), and was asked to create this issue._

By default Node, and evidently also Bun, resolves imports inside symlink'd files/folders differently than TypeScript's default.

TypeScript:
- resolve imports inside symlink'd files/folders relative to the path of the symlink

Node (by default) and Bun:
- resolve imports inside symlink'd files/folders relative to the path of the original file

However, Node has two ways to switch from the default behavior:
1. `node --preserve-symlinks myfile.ts`
2. `NODE_PRESERVE_SYMLINKS=1 node myfile.ts`

Is there any equivalent in Bun, and if not is there a workaround or is this on the roadmap?

Reference:
https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v20.x/api/cli.html#--preserve-symlinks

Glad to see https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/4340 in canary! I've run into the following issue with the initial implementation:

### What version of Bun is running?

0.8.2+9334fbe9b4facdfa9057a25e88e998f1fd2e346a

### What platform is your computer?

macOS Ventura 13.5.1

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
import { mkdir, cp, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

// Set up
await mkdir("./a/", { recursive: true });
writeFile("./a/foo.txt", "hello world");
await mkdir("./b/", { recursive: true });

// Copy from `./a/` to `./b/c/`
await cp("./a/", "./b/c/", { recursive: true });
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A folder at `./b/c/` is created, containing `foo.txt`.

(This is what `node` does. Note that both paths have trailing slashes, so they unambiguously refer to folders and not files.)

### What do you see instead?

```
ENOENT: No such file or directory
   path: "./b/"
 syscall: "clonefile"
   errno: -2
```

### Additional information

For a "real-world" case, try:

```shell
git clone https://github.com/lgarron/barely-a-dev-server && cd barely-a-dev-server
git checkout 79f70b086365a54b3b7fe7f09e3cc34dcd96cf17
bun run ./test/build.js
```

On [this line](https://github.com/lgarron/barely-a-dev-server/blob/923c708a0f2a0c17cd5ec5d5a99aade28d12ac0b/src/index.js#L28) it should be copying the contents of `./test/root/` to `dist/test/root/` but instead it errors with:

```
ENOENT: No such file or directory
   path: "dist/test/ro"
 syscall: "clonefile"
   errno: -2
```

Note that:

- The error shows a truncated path of `dist/test/ro`
- Even if `dist/test/root` exists, it is *deleted* by `bun`(!) instead of having files copied to it.

```ts
test.each(

  [3, 4],

    'should ...',

  );
```

```ts
describe.each(
  [1, 2],
  [3, 4],
  )(
    'something',
```

```ts
describe.only.each(...)(...) // Error!
```

title: Offer a sharding feature similar to jest to scale tests horizontally

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: bun:test
labels.description: Something related to the `bun test` runner

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun is fast, but even the fastest can become overwhelmed with a large enough suite of tests. Slow unit tests is a problem.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Spread the test workload evenly across multiple machines in CI similar to [jest's --shard flag](https://jestjs.io/docs/next/cli#--shard) and only use `--watch` mode or `--changedSince=master` flags to run tests that need to run based on changed files locally.

I just had to set this up on jest and it caused some headaches with coverage collection since you have to merge the coverage after all test shards are complete. I figured the Bun team may want to keep test sharding in mind as they develop and optimize their coverage collection and reporting mechanisms.

### What alternatives have you considered?

jest --coverage --shard=1/2------> |
---------------------------------------|-------> nyc merge ... && nyc report ...
jest --coverage --shard=2/2 ------>|

title: QOL Improvement: Support Automatically Managing Type Definitions

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

TypeScript developers need to manually install and uninstall type definitions for packages using `bun add @types/<package-name> -D`. The process can look something like this

1. Install a new package.
2. Wait for installation (1, 2 seconds at most)
3. Import the new package
4. Encounter TypeScript errors due to missing type definitions.
5. Manually run `bun add @types/<name> -D` to install type definitions.
6. Wait again for type definition installation (1, 2 seconds at most)

A similar process exists when uninstalling, where forgetting to uninstall the type definitions is more common in my experience.

### Indication of interest

There are several utilities, Reddit, and StackOverflow posts for people asking if such functionality exists for other package managers[^1][^2][^3][^4][^5], and utilities for other package managers which do this[^6][^7][^8][^9]. While we could ask one of them to support Bun, native is always faster.

[^1]: https://www.reddit.com/r/typescript/comments/6d3m16/is_it_possible_to_automatically_npm_install/
[^2]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56623737/how-to-install-types-from-an-npm-package-that-has-in-its-name
[^3]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60339541/does-npm-or-yarn-have-feature-to-automatically-install-types-if-they-exist-in-t
[^4]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48857430/install-type-definitions-automatically-when-i-install-an-npm-package
[^5]: https://www.reddit.com/r/typescript/comments/9i4age/installuninstall_types_packages_automatically/?rdt=55158 
[^6]: https://github.com/jeffijoe/typesync
[^7]: https://github.com/xavdid/typed-install
[^8]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@yarnpkg/plugin-typescript
[^9]: https://github.com/T-Specht/ts-typie

### Potential Roadblock

What if a package has embedded type definitions but also an old `@types` package that does not have a deprecation flag?

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Bun would look up whether `@types/<package-name>` exists when installing a package. For example, if I run `bun add common-tags` Bun would also look up `@types/common-tags`, see that it exists, and install it.

There are two ways I see to configure this:
1. Explicit opt-in: `autoManageTypeDefinitions = true` in `bunfig.toml` (default to false)
2. Explicit opt-out: Same as above but default would be `true`
3. Prompt: If bun detects a type definitions package it asks `Install @types/<package-name>?`. Users would most likely still want a `bunfig.toml` option so they don't have to answer `yes` every time. Same for uninstalling: `Uninstall @types/<package-name>?`

### What alternatives have you considered?

1. Creating custom scripts to automate the installation of type definitions in Bun
2. Asking one of the aforementioned tools to add Bun support

title: Use nix to provide single command dev environment setup and reproducible builds

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

I want bun to succeed as an open source project. For that to happen, it should be easy for anyone hack on bun’s code base and contribute their improvements back. 

However [the instructions](https://bun.sh/docs/project/development) for setting up dev tooling are not very user friendly.

Image a js project without a `package.json` nor a lock file, which listed it’s npm deps in a README, some with version numbers others without. 

Setting up dev environment for bun should be as easy as running `npm install`. Same for building, testing etc. All deps needed for this should be pinned, just like we do for js projects with lock files.

How? Easy: just use [nix](https://nixos.org/). Drop a [flake.nix (together with flake.lock)](https://zero-to-nix.com/concepts/flakes) in your repo and anyone (on any linux or Mac machine) will be able to run:

1. `nix develop` - to drop into a development shell with all deps needed to build `bun` available and ready to use 
2. `nix build` - to build the `bun` binary (or fetch it from cache if available) 
3. `nix run` - to run the `bun` binary (built from source if a pre-built binary for current state of the repo is not available in local or remote cache)
4. `nix flake check` - to run all checks (tests, lint, format etc) you’d like devs to run before opening a PR

All of these transparently cached and perfectly reproducible.

You might even be able to use this to speed up your CI pipeline ;)

The only requirement for the users would be to install [nix](https://nixos.org/download#nix-install-linux). And hence your development setup instructions could be reduce to 2 lines of bash.

You could even provide a pre-configure instance of [nvim](https://github.com/nix-community/nixvim) or [vscode](https://github.com/nix-community/nix-vscode-extensions) with all tooling (extensions etc) configured and ready to go. 

Finally, for people who really like containers, you could have one built with just a few lines of nix. It would contain the exact same binaries (byte for byte) provided in the dev shell by `nix develop`.



 

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add a [flake.nix](https://zero-to-nix.com/concepts/flakes) defining all dev tools and scripts needed to contribute to bun’s development

### What alternatives have you considered?

Build a docker container with dev environment based on one of the popular distros Linux distros. Meh

title: Support 32-bit ARM CPUs (currently arm64 only)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

There are plenty of devices (especially embededd) that run arm 32 bit OSes, the most famous one is Raspberry PI. Bun looks like an excellent choise to run edge intelligence \ IoT servers, however at this time bun offers only arm64 binaries, which prevents it to be use on this vast plethora of OSes (very few embedded OSes are 64 bit) which power this small SBCs.

For instance, our OS (based on Debian) runs on about a dozen of such SBCs and just one of them has a vendor BSP with 64 bit kernel, therefore to maximize compatibility we only provide a 32 bit BSP. The same is true for Raspberry PI, which only offers 64bit kernel for just the version 4. 

IMHO reconfiguring the CI to provide arm binaries will open Bun to a wider userbase and usecases, given that it's architecture can allow for 32 bit operations. 

Happy to help outline such usecases and help where necessary.



### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Provide compiled binaries for arm platform, along with arm64 and x64

### What alternatives have you considered?

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.0.2

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 22.6.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create new Angular 16.x web application and try starting it with bun instead of node
2. During the spawning the local web server, the unhandled exception is raised with the reference for more details in the local file
3. Open the file and see the stack trace there.

### What is the expected behavior?

Local web server should start with no issues.

### What do you see instead?

Local web server launch fails with exception.

### Additional information

The stack trace for the exception is the following:

```
[error] Error: ipaddr: the address has neither IPv6 nor IPv4 format
    at <anonymous> (/Users/build/Projects/viewer/node_modules/ipaddr.js/lib/ipaddr.js:934:11)
    at logStatus (/Users/build/Projects/viewer/node_modules/webpack-dev-server/lib/Server.js:2883:31)
    at <anonymous> (/Users/build/Projects/viewer/node_modules/webpack-dev-server/lib/Server.js:3393:19)
    at processTicksAndRejections (:55:39)
```

(Btw, another issue here is that the line numbers are incorrect and point to unrelated lines, though they are somewhat close to the actual ones).

After digging into it a bit, it seems that bun and node return different values HTTP/HTTPS server address() method call.

Here is the code snippet from `Server.js` where the original data is fetched
```javascript
const { address, port } =
        /** @type {import("net").AddressInfo} */
        (
          /** @type {import("http").Server} */
          (this.server).address()
        );
```

It is later passed to the `ipaddr` in the following way:

```javascript
const parsedIP = ipaddr.parse(address);
```

So, when this code is run in node, address contains "127.0.0.1", whereas bun returns "localhost". `ipaddr` does not expect address to be aliased this way and fails.

title: Allow explicitly hoisting certain packages using `public-hoist-pattern`

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: bun install
labels.description: Something that relates to the npm-compatible client

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun, like pnpm, doesn't automatically hoist packages to the root `node_modules` folder. This is the right thing to do. However, there are a handful of scenarios where we genuinely do need to hoist transitive dependencies. One of those scenarios is when we use the [`better-typescript-lib`](https://github.com/uhyo/better-typescript-lib) package.

This package, as the name describes, provides better type definitions for the built-in typescript libraries. For example, it provides stricter type definitions for `JSON.parse`, `JSON.stringify`, and `fetch().json()`, which helps developers catch more bugs at compile time. All you need to do to use this library is install it. It provides the type definitions as transitive dependencies.

```
  /better-typescript-lib@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6):
    resolution:
      {
        integrity: sha512-LMFX7HPN5qlJiW5IlJiicTT2XcJJ8wRTq3D1YinmZzqNQ0lKX409EK+4cmkuMZTkfyZXBxOca29zvZwIGt9Q3Q==,
      }
    peerDependencies:
      typescript: ">=4.5.2"
    dependencies:
      "@typescript/lib-decorators": /@better-typescript-lib/decorators@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-dom": /@better-typescript-lib/dom@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2015": /@better-typescript-lib/es2015@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2016": /@better-typescript-lib/es2016@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2017": /@better-typescript-lib/es2017@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2018": /@better-typescript-lib/es2018@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2019": /@better-typescript-lib/es2019@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2020": /@better-typescript-lib/es2020@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2021": /@better-typescript-lib/es2021@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2022": /@better-typescript-lib/es2022@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2023": /@better-typescript-lib/es2023@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es5": /@better-typescript-lib/es5@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es6": /@better-typescript-lib/es6@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-esnext": /@better-typescript-lib/esnext@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-scripthost": /@better-typescript-lib/scripthost@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-webworker": /@better-typescript-lib/webworker@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      typescript: 5.1.6
    dev: true
```

These transitive dependencies, such as `@typescript/lib-es5`, are hoisted to the root `node_modules` folder by package managers like yarn and npm. And, when the TypeScript compiler sees `@typescript/lib-*` packages in the root `node_modules` folder it replaces the built-in type definitions for that library with the type definitions provided by the package. For example, the type definitions in `es5.d.ts` would be replaced by the type definitions provided by `@typescript/lib-es5`.

Unfortunately, because bun doesn't hoist packages, we can't use `better-typescript-lib` with bun. This is a shame, because `better-typescript-lib` is an indispensable package for me. I ❤️ both bun and `better-typescript-lib`. It would be awesome if I could use both of them together.

### References

- [`better-typescript-lib`: How it works](https://github.com/uhyo/better-typescript-lib#how-it-works)
- [TypeScript 4.5 Release Notes: Supporting `lib` from `node_modules`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-5.html#supporting-lib-from-node_modules)


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Like bun, pnpm also doesn't automatically hoist packages to the root `node_modules` folder. However, it does provide an escape hatch, [`public-hoist-pattern`](https://pnpm.io/npmrc#public-hoist-pattern), which can be used to hoist only certain packages. Thus, we can use `better-typescript-lib` with pnpm by adding the following line to our `.npmrc` file.

```
public-hoist-pattern[]=@typescript/*
```

I especially like this solution, because we're being explicit about which packages we want to hoist. And, as the [Zen of Python](https://peps.python.org/pep-0020/) states, "Explicit is better than implicit." It would be awesome if bun also implemented the `public-hoist-pattern` config option. Implementing something like `public-hoist-pattern` in the `bunfig.toml` file would be the easiest way to enable `better-typescript-lib` to be used with bun.

### References

- [`better-typescript-lib`: Installation with pnpm](https://github.com/uhyo/better-typescript-lib#with-pnpm)

### What alternatives have you considered?

There are three alternatives here.

1. 😢 Don't use bun. I would have to fall back to using pnpm again, which is not bad, but I would love to use bun.
2. 😭 Don't use `better-typescript-lib`. If I want to continue using bun then I'd have to give up on using `better-typescript-lib`, which is currently a deal-breaker for me.
3. 🤔 Change `better-typescript-lib` to somehow work with bun. labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: bun:test
labels.description: Something related to the `bun test` runner

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Allows developers to test a single test using `test.only` without having to use the `--only` flag.

This is particularly useful when testing with `bun test --watch` and debugging a single test. Having to stop and start bun to use `test.only` is time-consuming.

It would also match jest/vitest functionality.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

When a developer uses `test.only`, only those tests are run, regardless of if a flag is set. Otherwise testing proceeds as normal.

### What alternatives have you considered?

Switch between `bun test --watch` and `bun test --watch --only` as needed.

title: Bunx: support specifying package to install

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: bun install
labels.description: Something that relates to the npm-compatible client

labels.name: good first issue
labels.description: Something that would be good for new contributors

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

If the binary to run is not named same as the package, you won't be able to run it with `bunx`. There are some binaries included in packages that don't have same name as package. 

For instance, [Renovate]: a tool to update dependencies. Their package provides [two binaries](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/35.159.7/package.json#L6-L7):

1. `renovate` (same as package name) to run the dependencies update bot
2. `renovate-config-validator`: to validate your config


[Renovate]: https://www.mend.io/renovate/

You can run the bot with `bunx renovate`. But you can't run the `renovate-config-validator` using `bunx` right now. 

Other package managers offer the `-p` CLI option to specify which package to install, then the first argument is the binary to run. For instance, following previous example:

- **NPM offers [`npm exec --package`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-exec)/[`npx -p|--package`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npx)**
  We can run the script with:
  - `npm exec --package renovate renovate-config-validator`
  - `npx --package renovate renovate-config-validator`
- **Yarn (berry) offers [`yarn dlx -p|--package`](https://yarnpkg.com/cli/dlx#options)**
  We can run the script with:
  - `yarn dlx -p renovate renovate-config-validator`
 



### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Would be nice to have also some `-p` or `--package` to enable this use case :) 

### What alternatives have you considered?

Installing the dependency, then use `bun run` with path to script in `node_modules` directory. But the great of `bunx` is to just install and run for dependencies that won't be needed often. Like validating the configuration of your dependencies update tool.

Until then, other package managers can be used for this purpose

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.0.20+09d51486e

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.0.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use `execFile` or `execFileSync` to execute a script that produces no output. In my case, this is `osascript` with no return value.

Try this code:

```
const { execFile } = require("child_process")
const { promisify } = require("util")
const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)
execFileAsync('echo', ['>', '/dev/null']).then(({ stdout }) => console.log(typeof stdout))
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The result of the functions contains a `stdout` property. For an empty output, it should be an empty string. In Node.js, the above piece of code prints: "string".

### What do you see instead?

In Bun, if the output of the executable is empty, the value of `stdout` is `undefined`. Running the same piece of code in Bun prints "undefined".

### Additional information

This behavior is used here:
https://github.com/sindresorhus/run-applescript/blob/9db60e8a8fa7db46534c3c8a05c0f58135280ebb/index.js#L15

This is a popular package with 5 million downloads per week. Bun will break if the package is used to execute code with no return value; as the package tries to call `stdout.trim()`, which fails if `stdout` is `undefined`.

### What version of Bun is running? 1.0.25+a8ff7be64 ### What platform is your computer? Linux 5.15.0-91-generic x86_64 x86_64 ### What steps can reproduce the bug? Run the following code and try to open the PDF file created. ```JS const headless=true async function generatePDF() { const browser = await puppeteer.launch({ headless: headless ? 'new' : false }); const page = (await browser.pages())[0] // await page.setContent('

Hello, Puppeteer!

'); await page.goto('https://news.ycombinator.com/') await page.waitForSelector("body") await page.waitForNetworkIdle() await page.pdf({ path:'test02.pdf' }) await browser.close() } await generatePDF() ``` ### What is the expected behavior? A valid PDF created that can be opened by PDF readers. ### What do you see instead? A corrupt PDF file is created. When trying to open with Xreader I get: `PDF document is damaged`. Google Chrome (v120) says: `Failed to load PDF document.`. Midnight commander says: `Syntax Error: Couldn't find trailer dictionary` ### Additional information The same code when run with `node` generates a valid PDF file that can be opened by all readers. The simple page (commented out line) with the `Hello, Puppeteer!` H1 message generates a correct PDF file. Also tested with `.setContent` but with larger HTML code and the resulting PDF file was also corrupt. So it might be a buffering issue that only comes up when the content is larger. This issue might be related to https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/7728 but the manifestation is different (no error message, only a corrupt file generated). ### Workaround By replacing the line: ```JS await page.pdf({ path:'test02.pdf' }) ``` with: ```JS await Bun.write("test02.pdf", await page.pdf({})) ``` The generated PDF file will be valid.

Run any command with drizzle-kit using --bun, for example: `drizzle-kit generate:pg` or `drizzle-kit push:pg`. > I found another way to fix it. It's kind of working, but we can use export in schema.ts
First, go to node_modules/drizzle-kit/bin.js and find src/serializer/<your-driver>Imports.ts(pg for pgImports.ts and mysql for mysqlImports.ts).
And, change forEach statement in prepareFromExports or prepareFromMySqlImports(function that contains forEach) to for ... in statement.
The problem is that Bun's Object.values or Object.keys for the Module object (a return value of require) give us nothing unlike Nodejs.
const schema = require('./db/schema.ts')
const exports = Object.values(schema) // []
and somehow for ... in can iterate the object even in Bun.

For reproduction, feel free to use this repo: [dbest-stack](https://github.com/itsyoboieltr/dbest-stack)

4. Change the `push` script inside the `package.json` from `drizzle-kit push:pg` to `bun --bun drizzle-kit push:pg`
5. Run `bun push`
6. Watch your database disappear (lol)

### What is the expected behavior?

The db schema is pushed, migrations are generated.

### What do you see instead?

The db is dropped (on push), the migrations are not generated.

Seems to be something with Object.values or require?

title: Bun on Termux

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

body:
### What is the type of issue?

Documentation is missing

### What is the issue?

# Missing Docs for Termux users

## Intro
While the primary focus of Bun is not currently on Android platforms like Termux, this aims to help Termux users install and use Bun smoothly.

### installation
To begin, refer to the [official Bun installation documentation](https://bun.sh/docs/installation) using the following command:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
```
However, after installation, attempting to use Bun may result in a `Command not found` error.

## Solutions

### **Native Termux**
1. Start by addressing this issue with the only current viable solution — utilizing Termux's glibc package, which is detailed [here](https://github.com/termux-pacman/glibc-packages).
2. After installation, set an alias using `grun` to process the binary correctly.
-   Open your preferred configuration file (e.g., `vim ~/.zshrc`).
-   Add the alias:
```bash
alias bun="grun ~/.bun/bin/bun"
```
#### **Downsides**
While this solution has its usecases, there are some downsides to consider:

##### **Packages Are Limited:**
Due to limitations with `grun`, Bun may encounter difficulties reading and processing node modules, resulting in errors like:
```bash
❯ bun run index.ts
error: Cannot find package "some-package" from "/storage/emulated/0/Download/some_project/index.ts"
```
##### **Limited Functionality:**
As of now, due to native permissions and issues with `grun`, the Bun binary isn't fully processed. Consequently, certain operations may not work correctly:

- **Installing packages:**
```bash
❯ bun add axios
bun add v1.0.25 (a8ff7be6)  🔍 axios [6/6]error: FailedToOpenSocket downloading package manifest axioserror: axios@ failed to resolve
```

- **Using features like `bunx` or Bun's REPL:**
```bash
❯ bun repl
error loading current directoryerror: CouldntReadCurrentDirectory----- bun meta -----Bun v1.0.25 (a8ff7be6) Linux arm64 #1 SMP PREEMPT Wed Dec 27 11:31:51 UTC 2023BunxCommand:Elapsed: 11ms | User: 4ms | Sys: 12msRSS: 33.55MB | Peak: 9.72MB | Commit: 33.55MB | Faults: 12----- bun meta -----0   0x720c4e24f81   ???2   ???3   ???4   ???5   ???6   ???Search GitHub issues https://bun.sh/issues or ask for #help in https://bun.sh/discord
```
#
### **Proot distro**
For installation and usage of Bun on Termux with a better approach, follow these steps:
1. **Install PRoot-Distro:**
Execute the following command to install PRoot-Distro using Termux's packages:
```bash
apt update && apt install proot-distro -y
```
2. **starting a session**
```bash
proot-distro install ubuntu proot-distro login ubuntu # once installed you can use this anytime to start your Ubuntu terminal
```
3. **make sure bun is installed in the new session**
4. **After installation**, set an alias to run the Bun binary. Unlike native Termux, there are no external packages needed in this environment.
-   Open your preferred configuration file (e.g., `vim ~/.zshrc`).
-   Add the alias:
```bash
alias bun="~/.bun/bin/bun" # Or use the path where you have placed Bun's binaries
```
5. **Restart Your Shell**:
If you're using zsh, restart your shell to apply the changes:
```bash
exec zsh
```
6. **Verify Installation**:
Confirm the successful installation of Bun by running:
```bash
bun --version
```
#### **downsides**
- **Installing Packages**:
Due to Bun not being optimized for Android architectures, it lacks the necessary permissions to access node_modules. However, a fix is available. Update your configuration file with the following:
```bash
alias bun=bun_function
# Function to handle installations with the "--backend=copyfile" flag to prevent an "access denied" error during package installations.
bun_function() {
  if [ "$1" = "add" ]; then
    shift
    ~/.bun/bin/bun add --backend=copyfile "${@}"
  else
    ~/.bun/bin/bun "$@"
  fi
}
```
## **Additional Notes**
This **doesn't** intend to force developers to prioritize Termux support but serves as a guide for those with limited access to environments like Termux. Ideas and fixes presented here are mostly original, with clarifications drawn from insightful comments on related issues.

## **credits:**
Special thanks to issue #5085 for providing insights into fixing package installations. Additionally, credit goes to **[Denos fix](https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/4862#issuecomment-1049502951)** for addressing similar usage issues.

# Where Did You Find It?
This issue post aims to address missing documentation for Bun on Termux. It is *not intended to compel developers to prioritize Termux support but rather serves as guidance for users with limited access to environments like Termux. The outlined solutions and insights are derived from mostly original ideas with additional clarification from comments on related issues, particularly issue #5085 and [Denos fix](https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/4862#issuecomment-1049502951).

labels.name: node.js

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.0.27+c34bbb2e3

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.7.4-arch1-1 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Simple passthrough from stdin to stdout:
```ts
import { Readable, pipeline, PassThrough } from 'node:stream'

pipeline(
    Readable.toWeb(process.stdin),
    new PassThrough(),
    process.stdout,
    () => { },
)
```

Independently of how you split it with the blocksize:
`dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1 count=16383 | bun run <file>.ts > /dev/null`: works without any issues
`dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1 count=16384 | bun run <file>.ts > /dev/null`: writes all the data to stdout, but the process hangs forever intead of stopping when stdin closes

I believe it's stdin read, as the limit is always that, even applying compression to the algorithm.

### What is the expected behavior?

Process should exit normally when stdin closes, just like it does with < 16KiB data, node behaves the same.

I noticed tho, that this slight modification seems to prevent the bug:
```ts
import { Readable, pipeline, PassThrough } from 'node:stream'

pipeline(
    Bun.stdin.stream(),
    new PassThrough(),
    process.stdout,
    () => { },
)
```
(TS types are broken tho)

### What do you see instead?

The process hangs

### Additional information

~~A side note, isn't the callback function on pipeline supposed to be optional?~~
~~At least according to the types, excluding it doesn't cause any issue on my IDE but the code breaks:~~
~~`TypeError: The "streams[stream.length - 1]" property must be of type function. Received an instance of EventEmitter`~~
Node behaves the same, but the types shouldn't be like that imo... it's nodejs's side anyways.

title: Regression in Bun.$ subprocess interactivity with @inquirer/prompts in v1.0.31

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: shell
labels.description: Something to do with Bun as a shell

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.0.31+e25675121

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.2.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use Bun to run a script that spawns a Node.js subprocess which invokes [@inquirer/prompts](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@inquirer/prompts) (v4.3.0) for user interaction.

1. The subprocess attempts to use the select function to prompt the user to choose between predefined options.
2. Observe the behavior when running the script using Bun version 1.0.30.
3. Repeat the observation with Bun version 1.0.31.

Code to reproduce:
```javascript
const program = `
const { select } = require('@inquirer/prompts');

async function run() {
  const foobar = await select({
    message: 'Foo or Bar',
    choices: [
      { name: 'Foo', value: 'foo' },
      { name: 'Bar', value: 'bar' },
    ],
  });
  console.log('Choice:', foobar);
}

run();
`;

await Bun.$`echo "Bun version: $(bun --version)"`;
await Bun.$`[ -t 0 ] && echo "[stdin] good" || echo "[stdin] bad"`;
await Bun.$`node -e ${program}`;
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The script is expected to display the prompt, allowing the user to interactively select either "Foo" or "Bar" using the arrow keys. The interactive functionality is expected to work consistently across different Bun versions, including v1.0.30 and v1.0.31.

### What do you see instead?

**v1.0.30**
Working as expected. The prompt is displayed, and the user can interact with it to make a selection.
```
Bun version: 1.0.30
[stdin] good
? Foo or Bar Bar
Choice: bar
```

**v1.0.31**
The prompt is displayed but does not respond to user input. The user is unable to select an option or otherwise interact with the subprocess.
```
Bun version: 1.0.31
[stdin] good
? Foo or Bar (Use arrow keys)
❯ Foo
```

### Additional information

Given the v1.0.31 changelog mentions significant changes to how subprocesses are spawned and file streaming is handled, it's possible these updates may have inadvertently impacted the handling of stdin/stdout/stderr streams in scenarios requiring terminal interaction. Both Bun versions confirm stdin is inherited and is connected to a terminal, so the regression might be related to changes in subprocess spawning behavior in v1.0.31.

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.0.35

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.4.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Here are the minimum steps to reproduce:

```sh
bun install eslint
echo '{ "plugins": ["unknown-plugin"] }' > .eslintrc.json

bun --bun x eslint . # Shows unclear error
npx eslint . # Shows understandable error
```

### What is the expected behavior?

This is the correct error output when running with Node:

<details>
    Oops! Something went wrong! :(

    ESLint: 8.57.0

    ESLint couldn't find the plugin "eslint-plugin-unknown-plugin".

    (The package "eslint-plugin-unknown-plugin" was not found when loaded as a Node module from the directory "…".)

    It's likely that the plugin isn't installed correctly. Try reinstalling by running the following:

        npm install eslint-plugin-unknown-plugin@latest --save-dev

    The plugin "eslint-plugin-unknown-plugin" was referenced from the config file in ".eslintrc.json".

    If you still can't figure out the problem, please stop by https://eslint.org/chat/help to chat with the team.

</details>

### What do you see instead?

This is the unclear error output when running with Bun:

<details>
    Oops! Something went wrong! :(

    ESLint: 8.57.0

    TypeError: Attempted to assign to readonly property.
        at _loadPlugin (…/node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:3452:12)
        at <anonymous> (…/node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:815:40)
        at reduce (:1:11)
        at _normalizeObjectConfigDataBody (…/node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:701:112)
        at _normalizeObjectConfigData (…/node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:676:26)
        at loadInDirectory (…/node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:622:111)
        at _loadConfigInAncestors (…/node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:1070:57)
        at getConfigArrayForFile (…/node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:1036:119)
        at _iterateFilesRecursive (…/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine/file-enumerator.js:131:62)
        at iterateFiles (…/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine/file-enumerator.js:73:47)
</details>

### Additional information

The issue occurs when ESLint overwrites the `error.message` value [on this line in `config-array-factory.js`](https://github.com/eslint/eslintrc/blob/fb8d7ffbb27214686318a07e16ac8878aaafc805/lib/config-array-factory.js#L1105) after failing to resolve a referenced plugin. Since the error object is a Bun ResolveMessage instance, the `message` property of which is read-only, this causes a different error, obfuscating what the issue actually is. For compatibility with NodeJS, that property should be writeable.

There is also [an open issue in ESLint](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/6730).

title: Expanding BunJS Beyond a Runtime to a Comprehensive Development Ecosystem

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

BunJS, currently known as a runtime, build tool, and package manager, has the potential to evolve into a multifaceted development ecosystem. This proposal seeks to explore the idea of extending BunJS's capabilities to encompass native app development for mobile and desktop platforms(ReactNative/Capacitor), IoT (Internet of Things) integration akin to CyonJS and Johnny-Five, and even transforming BunJS into a full-fledged programming language with compiled language features.

The proposed expansion of BunJS aims to address several key challenges and opportunities:

Streamlined Development: By integrating native app development capabilities, developers can leverage BunJS's familiar syntax and tooling to build mobile and desktop applications more efficiently, reducing the need for learning multiple programming languages and frameworks.

IoT Integration: Extending BunJS to support IoT development enables developers to leverage its strengths in simplicity and productivity to create IoT applications and devices, fostering innovation and interoperability in the IoT ecosystem.

Language Flexibility: Transforming BunJS into a programming language with compiled language features opens up new possibilities for performance optimization, code obfuscation, and platform compatibility, enhancing its appeal for a wider range of use cases and industries.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

The proposed features to expand BunJS into a comprehensive development ecosystem include:

Native App Development: Introducing tools and libraries within BunJS to facilitate the development of mobile and desktop applications, including UI frameworks, build pipelines, and deployment solutions tailored for various platforms.

IoT Integration: Integrating BunJS with IoT frameworks and protocols, providing APIs and abstractions for interacting with sensors, actuators, and other IoT devices, and offering tooling for IoT application development and deployment.

Language Enhancements: Enhancing BunJS's language features to support compilation to native code, static typing, and other characteristics typically associated with compiled languages, while preserving its ease of use and dynamic nature.

Implementation Details:
To achieve these goals, collaboration with the BunJS community and integration with existing technologies and standards in mobile development, IoT, and programming language design will be essential. The implementation may involve:

Research and Planning: Conducting feasibility studies, gathering requirements from stakeholders, and defining a roadmap for the evolution of BunJS into a comprehensive development ecosystem.

Feature Development: Iteratively implementing features and enhancements based on the roadmap, prioritizing key functionalities such as native app development, IoT integration, and language improvements.

Community Engagement: Encouraging participation and feedback from the BunJS community through forums, discussions, and contributions to ensure that the expanded ecosystem meets the diverse needs and expectations of developers.

title: Incorrect string interpolation of os.platform and os.release

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.3

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.4.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```javascript
import os from "node:os";

console.log(`${os.platform}`);
console.log(`${os.release}`);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node 21.7.3 via `node os_release_platform.js`:
```
darwin
23.4.0
```

Deno 1.42.3 via `deno run -A os_release_platform.js`:
```
darwin
23.4.0
```

### What do you see instead?

Bun via `bun os_release_platform.js`:
```
function () {
    [native code]
}
function release() {
    [native code]
}
```

### Additional information

Bun interpolates `os.platform` and `os.release` as code in strings, NOT as literal values as in Node and Deno.

For example, in [Oracle OCI SDK](https://github.com/oracle/oci-typescript-sdk/blob/b129bce29a5a9575bc5506f40bda59b718c0ba9f/lib/common/lib/headers.ts#L57), these values are used as strings to set HTTP headers.

The following code:
```javascript
headers.append(USER_AGENT_HEADER, userAgent);
```

breaks
```
50 |         let userAgent = appendUserAgent
51 |             ? `${clientInfo} (${platform}/${release}; Node/${nodeVersion}) ${appendUserAgent}`
52 |             : `${clientInfo} (${platform}/${release}; Node/${nodeVersion})`;
53 |         // Headers will always be replaced if they exist already
54 |         headers.append(USER_AGENT_HEADER, userAgent);
             ^
TypeError: Header '84' has invalid value: 'Oracle-TypeScriptSDK/2.84.0 (function () {
    [native code]
}/function release() {
    [native code]
}; Node/v21.6.0)'
```

Currently, more or less acceptable workaround to have OCI library working is the top level monkey patch those values:
```
import os from "node:os";
os.platform = "platform";
os.release = "release";
```

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.4+e134ed253

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.5.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

- Clone the [minimal reproduction repository](https://github.com/wesleycoder/bun-test) on the machine or Github Codespaces (tested there too, not working)
- Open on the repository on the terminal
- Install Bun
- Upgrade Bun to canary (optional, also broken on production version at the time of this issue submission)
- Run the following commands observing the outputs
```sh
bun run --filter 'a' test # should run the test command on the `packages/a` package
bun --filter 'a' test # should run the test command on the `packages/a` package 
bun --filter '*' test # should run the test command on both `packages/a` and `packages/b` packages 
```

### What is the expected behavior?

We should be able to provide the `--filter` flag as described on [the docs](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/cli/filter.md) and be able to run scripts of children packages.

### What do you see instead?

Despite validating the `workspaces` option on `package.json`, the `--filter` option is faulty when detecting the existence of the packages for running scripts and always returns `error: No packages matched the filter` 

### Additional information

I've tried on my machine (Macbook Pro 14, M1 2021, Sonoma 14.5 Beta) and on GH Codespaces (smaller spec).
Both environments fail both on install and on script runs.

This is a follow up on the feedback given [on this issue](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/2232#issuecomment-2060542929) that tracked the feature being implemented.

*Edit:* removing the intent of installing dependencies as it is out of scope.

body:
This issue tracks supporting DataDog's `dd-trace`, which is currently spread across a few different issues.

- `node:dgram` #1630

title: GBK encoding is not supported by TextDecoder

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.6+e58d67b46

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.5.0-28-generic x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a bun script and try to instantiate a new TextDecoder
```typescript
// This will fail with either gbk or GBK
const decoder = new TextDecoder('gbk');
```

### What is the expected behavior?

It should accept the gbk encoding as specified on the MDN web docs:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/TextDecoder

### What do you see instead?

```
TypeError: Unsupported encoding label "GBK"
 code: "ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE"
```

### Additional information

More about the GBK format:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GBK_(character_encoding)
It is still used over utf-8 by some chinese websites, not supporting it leads to wrongly decoded characters when using fetch for example

body:
### How can we reproduce the crash?

I have no idea yet. I had my fresh code process a million search results from an external API that indexes public storage bucket

I cannot give a detailed crash report yet as I didn't encounter it again. There's 10k pages of HTTP requests happening here divided over 5 webworkers that process data from the external API and insert it into SQLite using many async/awaits.

Too complicated to trace, and i've only seen it happen once, but i wanted to get the crash report to you. There's probably some memory leaks in my code still too 😁

title: Some Stripe API calls failing in production since upgrading from Bun 1.0.x to Bun 1.1.x

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### What version of Bun is running? 1.1.7+b0b7db5c0 ### What platform is your computer? Linux 5.15.60+ x86_64 unknown ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Make a minimal script to setup a Stripe client and make a call to get a Stripe connection token: ```ts const stripe = new Stripe(""); const res = await stripe.terminal.connectionTokens.create(); ``` 2. Deploy it within Docker container based off `oven/bun:1.1.7-debian` to Google Cloud Run ### What is the expected behavior? The call should work and return an object of the form: ``` { "object": "terminal.connection_token", "secret": "" } ``` ### What do you see instead? The call fails with an exception: ``` 23 | * StripeError is the base error from which all other more specific Stripe errors derive. 24 | * Specifically for errors returned from Stripe's REST API. 25 | */ 26 | export class StripeError extends Error { 27 | constructor(raw = {}, type = null) { 28 | super(raw.message); ^ error: Invalid JSON received from the Stripe API code: "undefined" at new StripeError (/app/node_modules/stripe/esm/Error.js:28:13) at new StripeAPIError (/app/node_modules/stripe/esm/Error.js:109:42) at /app/node_modules/stripe/esm/RequestSender.js:174:33 ``` Caused by: ``` { message: "Invalid JSON received from the Stripe API", exception: 91 | response += chunk; 92 | }); 93 | this._res.once('end', () => { 94 | try { 95 | resolve(JSON.parse(response)); 96 | } ^ SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token '<' at () at parse (native:1:1) at /app/node_modules/stripe/esm/net/NodeHttpClient.js:96:16 at emit (native:1:1) at endReadableNT (node:stream:2414:27) ``` ### Additional information The actual response from the Stripe API under the covers is: ```html 400 The plain HTTP request was sent to HTTPS port

400 Bad Request

The plain HTTP request was sent to HTTPS port
nginx
``` The URL of the API Stripe is actually calling to is to: ``` http://api.stripe.com:443/v1/terminal/connection_tokens ``` ^ Note the `http` but the port `:443`. It seems that before Bun 1.1.0, the `https` was being inferred because of the port (?) but on every version between 1.1.0 and 1.1.7 the `http` is being left causing this error upstream. It's worth noting that I cannot seem to reproduce this issue outside of GCP — it only seems to happen there. If I try to run the same Docker container on Orbstack locally, or the app directly on MacOS, all works fine — this is mystifying as I'm trying to make it reproducible for you but have really struggled to make it easier! Our company is encountering this issue in production which is blocking us from upgrading to Bun 1.1.x. Pinning to Bun 1.0.36 resolves the issue.

### What platform is your computer?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Write a simple code snippet that calls Prisma. Eg.

```js
async function doSomething() {
     console.log("Entry!");
     
     await prisma.someModel.findMany({});
     
     console.log("Exit!")
}
```

Then call this function by a non-awaited call.

```js
doSomething()
``` 

What happens is that the call to Prisma just fizzles out, and it exits the promise at that location. This is not how both regular Node and TS-Node behaves, as they will successfully completely call everything.

### What is the expected behavior?

The entry log should be called, the Prisma function executed, and the exit log should be called

### What do you see instead?

Only the entry log is called, no Prisma call to the database takes place

### Additional information

Does not happen with any other async call (from limited testing), only Prisma

title: CallbackJob prevents VM to exit when result of callback is an unresolved promise

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.10+5102a9443

### What platform is your computer?

Any platform, reproduces everywhere

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This simple code will result in frozen process

```js
setTimeout(() => new Promise(() => 0), 0);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Process exits immediately after setTimeout (which aligns with Node behavior)

### What do you see instead?

Process is stuck. For whatever reason if CallbackJob sees promise, it will subscribe and wait until it succeeds, and this is not always the case.

https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/af4e844b621e8c889d2d73c2cd12a7426516ebbf/src/bun.js/api/BunObject.zig#L3811

Potential solution is to deinit CallbackJob regardless of promise status

### Additional information

This bug affects Worker.terminate() - terminate() returns promise which will never complete if Worker is already terminated. #9998 is affected by this bug.

The fact that Worker.terminate() is not fulfilling promise is separate issue. Node fulfills promise every time, but with undefined status code in this case. In attempt to fix original issue's problem I fixed that in #11376

There's also (absolutely irrelevant to this issue, but still notable) difference in status codes - Worker.terminate() yields status code 0 when thread is actually terminated, whereas Node returns 1

title: Dead code elimination strips out code which is actually not dead

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body: ### What version of Bun is running? 1.1.10 ### What platform is your computer? Darwin 23.5.0 arm64 arm ### What steps can reproduce the bug? - clone https://github.com/sedubois/bun-dead-code-bug/tree/670cfa650f32429b754bdf846213e368526d3f3e - `bun run build` - open index.html in a browser - open the JS console ### What is the expected behavior? No JS error. ### What do you see instead? There is an error `Uncaught TypeError: class heritage EVENT is not an object or null`. The error is raised in maverick.js, a transitive dependency of Vidstack. An `EVENT` constant is defined just before the place where it is referenced `maverick/packages/maverick/src/std/event.ts`: https://github.com/maverick-js/maverick/blob/d72709f1e367265ab2465fa153c25d72d0b2c709/packages/maverick/src/std/event.ts#L17 The EVENT constant referred to in the error should be kept by bun in the bundle. ### Additional information I first [reported](https://discord.com/channels/742612686679965696/1237413629989621913/1237413629989621913) this to Vidstack, who responded _"This would be an issue with Bun, not Vidstack. It seems like they're too aggressively eliminating dead code and not checking if a variable is used in a class heritage."_

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use drizzle ORM with bun:sqlite

Joint 2 tables.

```JavaScript
import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/bun-sqlite'
import { Database } from 'bun:sqlite'
const db = drizzle(sqlite)

const smsToServer = await db
  .select({
    sms: smsToServerTable,
    sirene: sirenenTable,
  })
  .from(smsToServerTable)
  .leftJoin(sirenenTable, eq(smsToServerTable.fromSireneId, sirenenTable.id))
  .where(
    and(
      gte(smsToServerTable.timestamp, from.toDate()),
      lte(smsToServerTable.timestamp, to.toDate()),
    ),
  )
```

### What is the expected behavior?

I should get the joined result as I defined it.

### What do you see instead?

The result objects does have the correct structure, but the values are scrambled. 
So all values are there but for example the value for a timestamp is inside the id field.

### Additional information

There is already a stackoverflow post from another user: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78376844/drizzle-join-results-are-scrambled

title: Bun script crashes when trying to compile SASS styles

labels.name: crash
labels.description: An issue that could cause a crash

labels.name: windows
labels.description: An issue that is known to occur on Windows

body:
### How can we reproduce the crash?

Install the `sass-embedded` package and write a build script like

```ts
import { Glob } from "bun";
import { join } from "node:path";
import * as sass from 'sass-embedded';

const styleFiles = new Glob(join(import.meta.dir, "static/**/*.scss"));

const outDir = join(import.meta.dir, "dist");

for await (const file of styleFiles.scan()) {
	const contents = await Bun.file(file).text();
	const result = await sass.compileStringAsync(contents);
	await Bun.write(join(outDir, file.replace('.scss', '.css')), result.css);
}
```

with a single `style.scss` file

```sass
*,
*::before,
*::after {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
```

placed in `./static/styles` directory.

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.17+bb66bba1b

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22631.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts
const manifest = await pacote.manifest(spec.raw, opts);

const tarball = await pacote.tarball(manifest._resolved, {
  ...opts,
  Arborist,
  integrity: manifest._integrity,
});
```

```js
  static #heapLimit = Math.floor(getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit) // Infinite
```

### How can we reproduce the crash?

- I was doing a git rebase of a branch with a bun package lock file to one with a npm package lock file.
- After resolving a conflict with the package.json file, I ran `bun install --lock-only` and got the error.
- I was able to work around this by deleting the bun lockfile and node_modules folder and then running `bun install`. (I don't know if I needed to delete both.)

title: Add fast path for `Map` and `Set` in `deepEquals`

labels.name: performance
labels.description: An issue with performance

labels.name: jsc
labels.description: Related to an issue in JavaScriptCore

body: With the recent webkit upgrade, the fast path for `Map` and `Set` in `deepEquals` was removed due to the underlying implementation changing to `OrderedHashTable` in JSC. We should find a way to bring the fast path back. `JSSetIterator` and `JSMapIterator` might be a good place to start

### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.20+ae1948925

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 5.15.146.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

In Jest the following test passes:
```JavaScript
describe('Test expect.toThrow(expect.any())', () => {
  it('should throw an error', () => {
    expect(() => {
      throw new Error('error')
    }).toThrow(expect.any(Error))
  })
})
```
However in Bun the test fails with the following error:
```
4 | describe('Test expect.toThrow(expect.any())', () => {
5 |   it('should throw an error', () => {
6 |     expect(() => {
7 |       throw new Error('error')
8 |     }).toThrow(expect.any(Error))
           ^
error: expect(received).toThrow(expected)

Expected constructor: ExpectAny
Received constructor: Error

Received message: "error"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The expected behavior is that `expect.toThrow()` should be using the return value of the function `expect.any()`.

### What do you see instead?

_No response_

### Additional information

I've tested this multiple times and created a project without any libraries to test it in Jest and in Bun. The issue is specifically with the behavior of `expect.toThrow(expect.any())`.
